title: The while Loop
objective: Repeat code with a while loop until its condition becomes false.

sourceAlignment.title: JavaScript Crash Course
sourceAlignment.author: Nick Morgan
sourceAlignment.note: Alignment metadata only; the conditional half of this book chapter is covered in Code Forge's Control Flow chapter. Lesson prose and exercises are original Code Forge material.

paragraphs: A while loop repeats a block of code for as long as its condition evaluates to true. Write while, a condition in parentheses, then a block in curly braces — the block runs again and again, re-checking the condition each time, until the condition is false.

Something inside the loop needs to eventually make the condition false, usually by changing a variable the condition depends on. If nothing does, the loop repeats forever and the program never moves on.
Use a while loop when you know the condition that should stop the repetition, but not necessarily how many times it will run.
explanation.rule: while (condition) { ... } keeps running its block until condition becomes false — something inside the loop must eventually make that happen.

examples.title: Countdown
examples.note: Each pass reduces count. Once it reaches 0, the condition is false and the loop ends.

checks.question: Why does a countdown loop eventually stop?
options: JavaScript automatically limits while loops to five passes.
The counter changes until the loop condition becomes false.

feedback.correct: Correct — the changing counter eventually makes the condition false.
feedback.incorrect: Not quite. Look for the value that changes each pass.

assignment.title: Forge Countdown
assignment.brief: Write forgeCountdown(start) using a while loop. Log every number from start to 1, then log FORGE!.
requirements: Do not use a for loop.
Log each number from start down to 1.
Log FORGE! after the loop ends.

hints: What value should change on every pass through the loop?
Your condition can stay true while the counter is greater than zero.
Log the counter, then subtract one from it.
FORGE! belongs after the loop has finished.
